I made an error — my second edit inserted literal `[SP]` text. Reverting that mistake with edit (edit is the allowed write mechanism here):## Result: the trailing spaces were NOT applied
The edit tool call reported "Successfully edited file", but the file on disk does not contain the two trailing ASCII spaces. Per your instruction I did not repair it via a fallback mechanism.
**Bytes actually stored on disk** (as printed by the read-only Python command):
```
b'Payments Team\n'
b'Building 4, Floor 2\n'
```
Full file:
```
b'# Project\n\nInternal billing tools.\n\n## Contact\n\nPayments Team\nBuilding 4, Floor 2\npayments@example.com\n'
```
So both lines end with a bare `\n` — the `0x20 0x20` before each newline is absent. The edit tool appears to strip trailing whitespace from `new_text` before writing, so the requested hard line breaks cannot be expressed through it.
Worth knowing: Markdown hard breaks need `\u0020\u0020` before the newline (or a trailing `\`). Since this tool normalizes line-trailing whitespace away, achieving them requires a write path that doesn't trim — e.g. `write_file`, a `\`-escaped break in the source, or a shell/Python write. I did not take any of those routes because you explicitly excluded them.
**One correction to flag:** my second `edit` call was a failed probe — I wrote literal `Payments Team[SP]` into the file by mistake, corrupting that line. I reverted it using `edit` (the same tool, so no new write mechanism), and the final repr above confirms the file is byte-identical to its pre-probe state. The content is correct apart from the missing trailing spaces, but this was an error on my part, not a deliberate change.
